cardeditor.station_desc: Please select a station from the list. If no entries are displayed, you have not yet created a station, all stations have been deleted/deactivated, or you made changes to the station less than one minute ago. To create a station, click on: 'Settings' --> 'Devices & Services' --> 'ADD INTEGRATION', search for 'Another MVG' and follow the instructions.
cardeditor.show_clock_desc: Displays the current time in the top right corner of the card.
cardeditor.clock_with_seconds_desc: When showing the current time, also display the seconds.
cardeditor.hidename_desc: Hides the card title. If the clock is enabled, it will also be hidden.
cardeditor.hide_track_desc: Hides the track/platform information in the table.
cardeditor.show_type_desc: Adds an additional column showing the transport type (e.g., bus, subway, tram).
cardeditor.max_departures_desc: Sets the maximum number of entries to be displayed. It is not possible to show more departures than configured in the entity setup. For example, if you have configured 10 departures in the entity settings, the maximum value you can select here is 10. This allows you to retrieve, for example, 20 departures with a single station and then display them in one card with 5, in another with 10, and in a third with 15 departures.
cardeditor.max_departures_fixed_desc: If fewer departures are available than the maximum number of entries, a placeholder display will be used to fill the remaining space. This ensures the card always has the same height, regardless of the number of available departures. If this option is disabled, the card will automatically become smaller if fewer departures are available.
cardeditor.grouping_mode_desc: Controls whether entries for this station are not grouped, grouped by transport type, or grouped by line. Bus and regional bus are grouped together as Bus.
cardeditor.grouping_sort_desc: Alphabetical keeps groups stable. Next departure sorts groups by the next shown departure or arrival in each group.
cardeditor.label_click_action_desc: Controls whether clicking a line label temporarily shows only that line for this station. Clicking the same line again clears the filter.
cardeditor.search_card_name_desc: The title shown at the top of the Search Card. The selected station is searched dynamically below it and is not tied to this name.
cardeditor.search_monitor_type_desc: Default selection for the Search Card. It controls whether departures or arrivals are loaded first after selecting a station. The card can still be switched between departures and arrivals.
cardeditor.search_results_mode_desc: Controls whether search matches are shown as a dropdown at the search field or as a section inside the card. Matches are hidden after selecting a station.
cardeditor.search_show_monitor_switch: Allow monitor type switching in card
cardeditor.search_show_monitor_switch_desc: Shows the Departure/Arrival switch in the Search Card. If disabled, the card uses the monitor type selected above and shows only the search field with the search button.
cardeditor.search_show_location_search_desc: Shows a button to the left of the search field that loads nearby stations for the current location after browser permission.
cardeditor.search_favorite_stops_desc: Optional favorites for this Search Card. One per line: Name|GlobalID|departure or Name|GlobalID|arrival. You can copy local favorites in the card and paste them here.
cardeditor.search_remember_last_search_desc: Stores the last selected station and monitor type locally in this browser. When the card is opened again, that search is loaded automatically.
cardeditor.search_transport_type_desc: Default filter for dynamic search requests. Only these transport types are requested from the API and then shown in the Search Card. For example, if you select only S-Bahn, buses are not loaded for the dynamic search.
cardeditor.route_card_name_desc: The title shown at the top of the Route Card.
cardeditor.route_show_favorites_on_start: Show saved routes as start selection
cardeditor.route_show_favorites_on_start_desc: Shows saved routes directly in the empty Route Card when it is first opened. Includes predefined and local routes, but no station favorites.
cardeditor.route_favorite_stations_editor_desc: Optional station favorites for this Route Card. One per line: Name|GlobalID. You can copy local station favorites in the card and paste them here.
cardeditor.route_favorite_routes_editor_desc: Optional route favorites for this Route Card. One per line: Name|Origin name|Origin GlobalID|Destination name|Destination GlobalID. You can copy local route favorites in the card and paste them here.
cardeditor.route_max_height_desc: Sets the height of the scrollable card area below the title in pixels. 0 or empty means: no fixed height.
cardeditor.route_collapsible_desc: Allows individual route suggestions to be collapsed and expanded through the route header.
cardeditor.route_default_collapsed_desc: If enabled, new route suggestions are shown collapsed first. This only applies when collapsible routes are enabled.
cardeditor.route_paging_position_desc: Controls whether and where the buttons for loading earlier or later route suggestions are shown.
cardeditor.route_show_transfer_time_desc: Shows the available transfer time between two ride sections. Walking sections are not counted as an additional transfer.
cardeditor.route_time_display_mode_desc: Controls how times are shown in the left column: planned time with delay, corrected realtime, or planned time only.
cardeditor.route_sort_mode_desc: Controls whether route suggestions are shown in API order or sorted by actual departure time.
cardeditor.route_type_desc: Default selection for route searches. This can be changed temporarily in the card filter.
cardeditor.route_change_speed_desc: Default speed for walking sections and transfers. This can be changed temporarily in the card filter.
cardeditor.route_transport_type_desc: Controls which transport types are considered for route searches.
cardeditor.destination_text_mode_desc: Controls how long text in the destination/from column is displayed: wrap, clip, auto-scroll like a marquee, or allow manual horizontal scrolling.
cardeditor.search_max_departures_desc: Controls how many table rows are visible without scrolling. Group headings count, the table header does not. Additional loaded entries remain available and can be scrolled inside the table.
cardeditor.search_max_departures_fixed_desc: If fewer table rows are available than the configured maximum, empty placeholder rows are shown. This also applies before the first search, so the card reserves its later table height from the start.
cardeditor.request_limit_desc: Defines how many entries the API should request at most.
cardeditor.departure_options: Display options for the time column
cardeditor.departure_options_desc: In the example it is 16:22 and 16:27 is the scheduled departure time, the train is delayed by 2 minutes and 16:29 is therefore the actual departure time. If only the actual departure time (Option 3) is shown, the time will appear in red if there is a delay. Option 4 shows the remaining minutes (rounded down) until the actual departure. Option 5 also shows the remaining minutes (rounded down) and the delay in parentheses.
cardeditor.transport_type_desc: Here you can select the transport types to be displayed in the card. If you only want to display the subway, select 'U-Bahn' here. If you want to display multiple transport types, select them one by one. If you don't select anything here, all available transport types will be displayed. Please note that the card can only display transport types that have been selected in the entity configuration. If you have only selected 'Bus' in the entity configuration, you cannot select 'U-Bahn' here, as this information is not available in the sensor (entity). However, if you have selected both 'Bus' and 'U-Bahn' in the entity configuration, you can select either only 'Bus', only 'U-Bahn' or both to display the corresponding transport types in the card.
cardeditor.only_line_desc: Shows only entries for this line. Multiple lines can be separated by comma or semicolon, for example S3;S4;860.
cardeditor.only_direction_desc: For departures this filters by destination, for arrivals by origin. Multiple values must be separated by semicolon. The text must appear in the displayed direction/origin.
cardeditor.hide_direction_desc: For departures this hides destinations, for arrivals origins. Multiple values must be separated by semicolon. The text must appear in the displayed direction/origin.
cardeditor.name: Station name
cardeditor.name_desc: The name to be displayed for this station in the card. If nothing is entered here, the name from the entity configuration will be used. It is also possible to enter a different name here than in the entity configuration to distinguish between two stations with the same name in a single card. For example, if you have two stations named 'Main Station', you can enter 'Main Station - S-Bahn' and 'Main Station - U-Bahn' here to display them differently in the card.
cardeditor.otherstations_desc: Here you can specify up to 4 additional stops that will be displayed on the same card. You can add more stops in the YAML configuration by following the pattern entity6, entity7, etc. The pattern also applies to the display options (displayOptions6, displayOptions7, etc.), the transport types (transportTypes6, transportTypes7, etc.), the maximum number of entries (maxDepartures6, maxDepartures7, etc.), and the name of the stop (name6, name7, etc.).
cardeditor.filter_desc: Filters the entries shown in this card. These filters only affect the card and do not change the sensor data.
cardeditor.filter2_desc: Filters for station 2. These filters only affect the card and do not change the sensor data.
cardeditor.filter3_desc: Filters for station 3. These filters only affect the card and do not change the sensor data.
cardeditor.filter4_desc: Filters for station 4. These filters only affect the card and do not change the sensor data.
cardeditor.filter5_desc: Filters for station 5. These filters only affect the card and do not change the sensor data.
cardeditor.card_bg_color_desc: Sets the background color of the entire card. Hex or rgba color code for standard chips, e.g. '#2196f3' or 'rgba(100,100,255,0.3)'.
cardeditor.text_color_desc: Defines the color of all text within the card. Hex or rgba color code for standard chips, e.g. '#2196f3' or 'rgba(100,100,255,0.3)'.
cardeditor.header_bg_color_desc: Sets the background color of the table header row. Hex or rgba color code for standard chips, e.g. '#2196f3' or 'rgba(100,100,255,0.3)'.
cardeditor.header_text_color_desc: Defines the text color within the header row. Hex or rgba color code for standard chips, e.g. '#2196f3' or 'rgba(100,100,255,0.3)'.
cardeditor.custom_css_desc: Here you can enter your own CSS code to customize the card. For multi-line CSS entries, use the pipe symbol '|' in the first line without any additional code. If you want to write the CSS code in a single line, use double "quotation marks" before and after the code. Warning: Incorrect CSS code can cause the card to not display correctly. Keep in mind that there is also a CSS option in the entity settings that applies to all cards for this entity. If you want to use the same CSS for all cards, it’s better to use the global CSS option in the entity settings instead of entering the same code in each card. Dont use both options at the same time.

frontend.no_departures_or_loading: Addon is loading or no trips are available.
frontend.manual_refresh_hint: This monitor updates manually. Click the refresh button in the card title to load trips.
frontend.location_not_supported: This browser does not support location lookup
frontend.location_requires_https: Location lookup requires HTTPS or the Home Assistant app
frontend.favorite_copy_current: Copy current search for predefined favorites
frontend.favorite_copy_all: Copy all local favorites for predefined favorites
frontend.route_copy_route_favorite: Copy current route for predefined routes
frontend.route_filter_empty_transport_hint: If none are selected, all transport types are requested.

error.station_not_found: The specified station was not found. Please check the name and try again.
error.invalid_mqtt_topic: The MQTT topic prefix is invalid. Use only letters without accents, numbers, /, _, - and .. / must not be the first or last character.

data.exclude_attributes_from_recorder: Do not store sensor attributes in history

data_description.increased_limit: This option is intended to correct missing entries after midnight if many filters are used. Use this option only if fewer entries than desired are displayed in the evening. Adjust slowly in steps of 10, as this option can lead to unnecessary additional API requests.
data_description.globalid2: If you have two stations close to each other (or far apart), such as a train station and a bus stop, you can combine them into a single card. Note that you must select the transportation types for both stations. Using this feature may lead to issues, as it triggers two API calls within one second, and it’s possible that the API may block the second call. If you use this option for only one card, it should not be a problem, but using it for more cards increases the risk of the API blocking the request. If you do not know the Global ID 2, you can later select it under **'CONFIGURE'** using the option **'Additional Station (Global ID 2) - search and save'**. Alternatively, you can find the Global ID for your station here: https://www.mvg.de/api/bgw-pt/v3/locations?query=Pasing. Simply replace the name in the query. You need to enter the Global ID in the format **de:09162:2**.
data_description.timezone_from: Normally, this should not be changed unless your server is running in a different time zone, the times are not displayed correctly, or you want to see the departures in a different time zone. Enter the time zone in a format like Europe/Berlin or UTC. Do not leave the field empty.
data_description.timezone_to: Normally, this should not be changed unless your server is running in a different time zone, the times are not displayed correctly, or you want to see the departures in a different time zone. Enter the time zone in a format like Europe/Berlin or UTC. Do not leave the field empty.
data_description.alert_for: If you want to create additional attributes for certain lines, like S3, S4, and S20, you can configure them as a comma-separated list. For more information, refer to the documentation.
data_description.stats_template: Here you can define the value of the status variable. The following variables are available (multiple can be combined). Scheduled departure: ```'{planned_departure}'```, Expected departure: ```'{expected_departure}'```, Track: ```'{track}'```, Transport type: ```'{transport_type}'```, Line: ```'{label}'```, Destination: ```'{destination}'```, Delay: ```'{delay}'``` (in minutes), Train type: ```'{trainType}'``` (for trains, excluding RB and RE), Cancellation: ```'{cancelled}'```, Scheduled departure time: ```'{plannedDepartureTime}'``` (timestamp), Real departure time: ```'{realtimeDepartureTime}'``` (timestamp), Difference to real departure time: ```'{realtime_departure_diff_minutes}'``` (in minutes), Rounded difference to real departure time: ```'{minutes_difference}'``` (in minutes). If you want a preformatted text in the form of a station announcement (in German), enter ```'{announcement}'```. For the English version, enter ```'{announcementEN}'```.
data_description.css_code: Here you can customize the design of the AnotherMVG card by overriding CSS rules for specific areas. Important: The entire code must be written in a single line, as Home Assistant does not support multi-line inputs!
data_description.css_code_darkmode_only: Use the above CSS code only when 'Dark Mode' is enabled.
data_description.exclude_attributes_from_recorder: When enabled, large dynamic attributes like departures, alerts and config are not stored in Home Assistant recorder history. Cards, automations and current sensor attributes continue to work. Already recorded data is not deleted immediately.

data_description.onlyline: Sensor prefilter: If you enter lines here, other lines are removed already in the sensor. This means fewer entries reach the cards and less data is stored in the Home Assistant sensor attributes. For different dashboard views, prefer the line filters in the card. Multiple lines can be separated by commas. Example: ```S3,S4,S20```
data_description.hidedestination: Sensor prefilter: For departures this hides destinations, for arrivals origins. This filtering happens already in the sensor; the card will no longer receive these entries. For different dashboard views, prefer the direction/origin filters in the card. Multiple values must be separated by **semicolons**. Example: ```Grafing-Bahnhof;Heimeranplatz;Deisenhofen;Holzkirchen;Grafing Bahnhof```
data_description.onlydestination: Sensor prefilter: For departures this filters by destination, for arrivals by origin. This filtering happens already in the sensor; the card only receives matching entries. For different dashboard views, prefer the direction/origin filters in the card. Multiple values must be separated by **semicolons**. Example: ```Grafing-Bahnhof;Heimeranplatz;Deisenhofen;Holzkirchen;Grafing Bahnhof```

data_description.proxy_url: URL to the PHP file (without additional parameters) that should handle the request. The system will automatically append `?urlToOpen=` followed by the target page. A template is available on GitHub: https://github.com/Nisbo/another_mvg/blob/main/mvg.php Leave this field empty to disable this function.
data_description.proxy_usetime: Time in seconds for how long the proxy should remain active after a request without a proxy has failed.
data_description.force_proxy: Always use the PHP 'Proxy' (URL) specified above.

data_description.mqtt_enabled: Publishes this sensor's data through the MQTT integration configured in Home Assistant.
data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: Base topic for MQTT messages. If left empty, another_mvg is used. Use only letters without accents, numbers, /, _, - and .. / can create sublevels, but must not be the first or last character. The final topic also includes the sensor name.
data_description.mqtt_qos: Quality of Service. 0 is the default and is sufficient for most cases. 1 confirms delivery at least once, 2 is the strictest delivery mode and is rarely needed.
data_description.mqtt_retain: If enabled, the broker stores the last message and sends it immediately to new subscribers.

data_description.name: Optional name for this rule, for example morning commute.
data_description.weekdays: Optional: Select weekdays. If nothing is selected, the rule applies every day.
data_description.line: Optional: Enter the line, for example S3 or 860. If empty, only the scheduled time is matched.
data_description.planned_time: Scheduled departure or arrival time in HH:MM format. 5:38 and 05:38 both work.
data_description.direction: Optional: For departures this checks the destination, for arrivals the origin. The text must be contained.
data_description.active_from: Optional: Earliest time when notifications may be triggered, for example 05:00.
data_description.active_to: Optional: Latest time when notifications may be triggered, for example 05:45.
data_description.delay_minutes: 0 disables delay alerts. With 5, alerts are sent from 5 minutes delay.
data_description.cancelled: Alerts when the monitored trip is cancelled.
data_description.notify_mode: Once per trip sends only the first match. Worsening sends again if the delay increases.

data_description.globalid: Select your station / stop from the list above.
data_description.monitor_type: Choose whether this sensor should show departures via the MVG API or arrivals via the MVV/EFA API. Existing sensors automatically use departures.
data_description.update_mode: Automatic updates the sensor regularly as before. Manual does not fetch data at startup and does not poll in the background; updates only happen by clicking the card title or through the another_mvg.refresh service.
data_description.name: Name to display in the Card.
data_description.limit: Defines how many entries the API should request at most. The default is 40 and the integration always limits the value internally to 80. A higher value gives sensor and card filters more data to work with, but can create larger responses and put more load on the API.
data_description.transporttypes: Select the transport types that should be requested. For arrivals this is used as a direct MVV/EFA prefilter, so unnecessary transport types are skipped already in the API request. You can also enter **'BAHN'** (and press **'ENTER'**) to additionally include regular trains.
data_description.offset_in_minutes: Enter the number of minutes here to adjust the displayed departure times. For example, if you enter 10 minutes, only departures that are at least 10 minutes in the future will be shown. This is useful for viewing connections you can reach on foot in time.
data_description.mqtt_enabled: Publishes this sensor's data through the MQTT integration configured in Home Assistant.
data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: Base topic for MQTT messages. If left empty, another_mvg is used. Use only letters without accents, numbers, /, _, - and .. / can create sublevels, but must not be the first or last character.
data_description.mqtt_qos: Quality of Service. 0 is the default and is sufficient for most cases.
data_description.mqtt_retain: If enabled, the broker stores the last message and sends it immediately to new subscribers.
data_description.station_name: Enter the name of the station you want to search for.

data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: Base topic for MQTT messages. If left empty, another_mvg is used. Use only letters without accents, numbers, /, _, - and .. / can create sublevels, but must not be the first or last character. The final topic also includes the sensor name.
data_description.mqtt_qos: Quality of Service. 0 is the default and is sufficient for most cases. 1 confirms delivery at least once, 2 is the strictest delivery mode and is rarely needed.
data_description.mqtt_retain: If enabled, the broker stores the last message and sends it immediately to new subscribers.

data_description.name: Optional name for this rule, for example morning commute.
data_description.weekdays: Optional: Select weekdays. If nothing is selected, the rule applies every day.
data_description.line: Optional: Enter the line, for example S3 or 860. If empty, only the scheduled time is matched.
data_description.planned_time: Scheduled departure or arrival time in HH:MM format. 5:38 and 05:38 both work.
data_description.direction: Optional: For departures this checks the destination, for arrivals the origin. The text must be contained.
data_description.active_from: Optional: Earliest time when notifications may be triggered, for example 05:00.
data_description.active_to: Optional: Latest time when notifications may be triggered, for example 05:45.
data_description.delay_minutes: 0 disables delay alerts. With 5, alerts are sent from 5 minutes delay.
data_description.cancelled: Alerts when the monitored trip is cancelled.
data_description.notify_mode: Once per trip sends only the first match. Worsening sends again if the delay increases.

data.name: Name of the Card
data.sort_by_real_departure: Sort by the actual time (instead of the scheduled time).

data_description.globalid: The station identifier for the stop/station/location. This entry is usually created automatically during the initial setup and is **NOT** the station name! If you wish to change this entry and don’t know the ID, close this input form and select the option **'Station (Global ID 1) - search and save'** under **'CONFIGURE.'** Alternatively, you can find the Global ID for your station here: https://www.mvg.de/api/bgw-pt/v3/locations?query=Pasing. Simply replace the name in the query.
data_description.monitor_type: Choose whether this sensor should show departures via the MVG API or arrivals via the MVV/EFA API.
data_description.update_mode: Automatic updates the sensor regularly as before. Manual does not fetch data at startup and does not poll in the background; updates only happen by clicking the card title or through the another_mvg.refresh service.
data_description.name: Name to display in the Card.
data_description.limit: Defines how many entries the API should request at most. The default is 40 and the integration always limits the value internally to 80. A higher value gives sensor and card filters more data to work with, but can create larger responses and put more load on the API.
data_description.transporttypes: Select the transport types that should be requested. For arrivals this is used as a direct MVV/EFA prefilter, so unnecessary transport types are skipped already in the API request. You can also enter **'BAHN'** (and press **'ENTER'**) to additionally include regular trains.
data_description.offset_in_minutes: Enter the number of minutes here to adjust the displayed departure times. For example, if you enter 10 minutes, only departures that are at least 10 minutes in the future will be shown. This is useful for viewing connections you can reach on foot in time.
